publication was by Medwin in The Athenaeum ccl (11 August 1832) 522–3. Medwin there
implies that he was reproducing the poem from memory because he introduces it as one ‘of
which I remember some of the stanzas’, but it is certain that he was in fact working from the
MS. The poem is given complete, although with four substantive errors, added punctuation
(including some pointing, which in typical Medwin fashion misunderstands S.’s sense: see
notes), but, most tellingly, an invented line replacing the line in which S. names Jane as the
Magnetic lady, perhaps suggesting that the Athenaeum version was produced under her
approval, Mary still in 1832 being unaware of the existence of the poem. Medwin published
a slightly revised text in Medwin (1833), on which Mary based her text in 1839. It is highly
probable that Mary’s revised text in 1840 was informed by corrections supplied by Jane
